newsitem.title: ITALY: Rome airport operator price set for bourse takeoff.
newsitem.headline: Rome airport operator price set for bourse takeoff.

text.p: Italian airport operator Aeroporti di Roma (ADR) on Saturday readied for take-off on the Milan bourse when it set the issue price for its forthcoming flotation at 11,000 lire ($6.40) per share.

The price, fixed at a shareholders' meeting, came at the top of a range indicated in the company's sale prospectus of 8,000 to 11,000 lire and values ADR at 1.32 trillion lire ($764 million), the company said in a statement.
Italy's Stock Exchange Council had previously valued the share price at 8,500 lire.
"The price takes into account the indications of interest received from global coordinators at the roadshow," the statement said.

A minimum 41 percent of the company -- and up to 45 percent under a "green shoe" option if demand is strong -- is being sold in a public sale offer (OPV) on July 15 and 16. It is the first privatisation of an Italian airport operator.
Indebted state industrial holding Iri now owns 73.58 percent of the company, but its holding is set to fall to around 54 percent after the flotation.

Some 25 percent is held indirectly by the banks Lehman Brothers Holdings Plc, Italian bank Imi's LDV Holding B.V., Crediop B.V., UBS Capital B.V. and M.M. Warburg & Co., who have said they will be selling their stake.

ADR said 30 percent of the 49.2 million ordinary shares on sale would be offered to the public, five percent would be reserved for company employees, and 65 percent would be left for Italian and foreign institutional investors.
Managing Director Gaetano Galia said last week he expected the company, which runs Rome's two airports at Fiumicino and Ciampino, to make its stock market debut on July 24 or 25.
Galia said that by 1998 IRI "will no longer be the main shareholder", adding that a second tranche sale was planned but the amount had yet to be defined.
Aeroporti di Roma boosted its net profits by 61 percent in 1996 to 90 billion lire and increased its turnover 11 percent to 1.16 trillion lire.
Passenger levels increased by 8.9 percent in 1996 to 23.8 million and the airports had traffic of more than 260,000 aircraft and 267,000 tonnes of freight.
ADR is poised to cash in when thousands of Roman Catholics are expected to arrive in Rome for the Vatican's Holy Year celebrations in 2000.

The company has a development plan under way to upgrade its services and has said it is evaluating the possibility of taking stakes in other companies in the airport sector elsewhere in Italy and abroad. ($1=1,727 lire)
